clinical_knowledge.topic: Acromegaly (GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acromegaly (GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Pituitary MRI with gadolinium, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: enlarging hands and feet, coarsening facial features, and headaches over 3 years

Key HPI features: 48M noticed shoe size increased from 10 to 12 and wedding ring no longer fits over past 3 years. Also reports prominent forehead, jaw protrusion, deepening voice, excessive sweating, joint aches, and frontal headaches with mild lateral visual blurring.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 72, BP 148/92. Prominent supraorbital ridges, macroglossia, spade-like hands, prognathism. Confrontation visual field exam confirms bitemporal hemianopsia. Bloods: Serum IGF-1 elevated (>3x normal for age). 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) fails to suppress Growth Hormone (<1 ng/mL).
Relevant background/PMH: Sleep apnea, hypertension, impaired fasting glucose
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acromegaly (GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Simple weight gain/aging without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Visual field changes — suggests optic chiasm compression, needing urgent neurosurgical evaluation.
management_principles: Urgent neurosurgery referral for transsphenoidal tumor resection

Consider medical therapy if residual tumor post-op: a somatostatin analog such as Octreotide or Lanreotide first-line, or the growth hormone receptor antagonist Pegvisomant when IGF-1 remains uncontrolled
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 48M presenting with chronic progressive acral enlargement, facial coarsening, prognathism, hyperhidrosis, headache, and bitemporal visual field defects over 3 years.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 72, BP 148/92. Prominent supraorbital ridges, macroglossia, spade-like hands, prognathism. Confrontation visual field exam confirms bitemporal hemianopsia. Bloods: Serum IGF-1 elevated (>3x normal for age). 75g Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) fails to suppress Growth Hormone (<1 ng/mL).
reference_soap.assessment: Acromegaly secondary to GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma with optic chiasm compression.
reference_soap.plan: Pituitary MRI with gadolinium. Urgent neurosurgery referral for transsphenoidal tumor resection. Consider medical therapy if residual tumor post-op: a somatostatin analog such as Octreotide or Lanreotide first-line, or the growth hormone receptor antagonist Pegvisomant when IGF-1 remains uncontrolled.

learning_objectives: Recognize subtle chronic somatic changes characteristic of acromegaly
Correlate bitemporal hemianopsia with pituitary macroadenoma optic chiasm compression
Interpret IGF-1 screening and OGTT growth hormone suppression confirmation tests
Discuss multidisciplinary surgical and medical management of GH excess

teaching.one_liner: Excess growth hormone from a pituitary tumor in adulthood causes gradual enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial features, and when the tumor compresses the optic chiasm, it also causes visual field loss.
differentials: Familial gigantism (if onset before growth plate closure)
red_flags: Visual field changes — suggests optic chiasm compression, needing urgent neurosurgical evaluation

must_ask.say: How much has your shoe or ring size changed, and over how long?
Have people commented that your facial features look different?
Have you had any blurring or loss of your side vision?
Do you snore heavily, or have joint aches?

history.answer: Over the past three years, my hands and feet have been getting bigger, and my face looks like it is changing shape.
It started very gradually about three years ago, so slowly that I barely noticed until my shoes and ring stopped fitting.
The changes are in my face, forehead, lower jaw, hands, and both of my feet.
My shoe size went up from size ten to size twelve, and my jaw has pushed forward so my teeth do not line up right anymore.
It has been continuously getting worse year after year without ever pausing or reversing.
Nothing seems to make the swelling better or worse; it just stays enlarged all day and night.
I have dull headaches across my forehead, deep aches in my knees and fingers, and I sweat heavily even when it is cool.
No fever, no unexpected weight loss, and no chest pain or shortness of breath.
I have never had body changes like this before, and no doctor has evaluated this issue yet.
I tried taking over-the-counter ibuprofen for my joint aches and headaches, which dulls the pain for a few hours but does not change the swelling.
No unusual chemical exposures, new supplements, recent travel, or changes in my diet.
My loud snoring and daytime tiredness make work harder, and my hands feel clumsy when I handle small tools at construction sites.
history.topic: Impact on daily life and sleep

history.answer: I had to stop wearing my wedding ring two years ago because it was cutting off circulation, and none of my old work boots fit.
history.topic: Change in ring and shoe size

history.answer: My forehead ridge feels much thicker, my lower jaw sticks out, and people have remarked that my face looks coarser and wider.
For the past few months, things on the outer edges of my vision have seemed blurry, like I am losing my side vision.
I get persistent, dull frontal headaches almost every week that throb across my brow.
My wife says my snoring has become unbearable and that I sometimes stop breathing, plus my knees ache constantly.
My voice has definitely gotten deeper and more hollow sounding over the past couple of years.
I sweat excessively day and night, drenching through my work shirts even in air-conditioned rooms.
I have had carpal tunnel-like numbness and tingling in both hands, mostly in my thumbs and index fingers.
I feel chronically fatigued and sluggish, though my muscle strength itself feels mostly intact.
No cold intolerance, though I definitely cannot tolerate heat because of how heavily I sweat.
My sex drive has dropped noticeably over the last year or two, which is unusual for me.
I assumed I was just gaining weight, getting older, and developing regular arthritis.
I am really worried about why my side vision is blurring and why these headaches will not go away.
I want to understand what is causing my facial bones and body structure to change so drastically.
I have obstructive sleep apnea, high blood pressure, and my primary doctor said I have borderline high blood sugar.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I take losartan fifty milligrams once daily in the morning for my high blood pressure.
I do not have any known drug allergies.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any nicotine products.
I drink two or three beers on the weekend with friends, but nothing during the work week.
I work as a construction manager, and I live at home with my wife and two teenage kids.
My father had hypertension and a stroke in his seventies, and my mother has type two diabetes, but nobody had hormonal or growth problems.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 148/92 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8 C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Coarsened facial features with prominent supraorbital ridges, broad nose, thickened lips, and obvious prognathism.
Confrontation visual field testing demonstrates bitemporal hemianopsia, while visual acuity is preserved.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light, with normal extraocular movements and no papilledema on funduscopy.
Marked macroglossia with lateral teeth imprints, widened interdental spaces, and soft tissue crowding of the oropharynx.
Thyroid gland is normal in size and texture, without palpable nodules, bruits, or tenderness.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal heart sounds S1 and S2, without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds and no crackles or wheezes.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender without palpable organomegaly or masses.
Hands are enlarged and spade-like with widened fingers, showing mild crepitus in the knees bilaterally without synovial effusion or redness.
Marked enlargement of both feet with heel pad thickening, but no pitting edema or calf tenderness.
Skin feels thick, oily, and doughy with noticeable generalized moistness from hyperhidrosis, but no skin tags or rashes.
